key_insight: The paper generalizes stabilizer bootstrapping from qubits to odd-prime qudits, giving the first efficient agnostic learner for qudit stabilizer states under realistic noise.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to characterize noisy qudit devices and estimate quantum state magic via stabilizer fidelity, which is useful for error correction and fault-tolerant quantum engineering.
method: Uses a stabilizer bootstrapping framework adapted to qudit structure.
Relies on single-copy and four-copy measurements only.
Includes a streamlined high-fidelity regime algorithm for \u03c4 > cos^2(\u03c0/8).
evidence_signal: From the abstract, the algorithm outputs a stabilizer state |\u03c6\u27e9 with fidelity at least \u03c4-\u03b5 to the unknown state using high probability, with sample/time complexity scaling as (d/\u03c4)^{O(d^2 log(1/\u03c4))} · poly(n,1/\u03b5).
watch_item: The stated complexity depends exponentially on d^2 log(1/\u03c4) and assumes odd-prime qudit dimension, so scaling and hardware support may be limiting in practice.
paper_title: Agnostic learning of qudit stabilizer states
